identification: Atom's Connections 1.7.1 beta, Ultra Encode, LLC; managed Windows launcher and embedded browser application
basis: Traced all 17 managed methods with dnfile/dncil; no module initializer, P/Invoke map, native payload, or overlay found.
Main calls Run. Run listens on 127.0.0.1/localhost:47800 by default and opens that URL with ProcessStartInfo.UseShellExecute=true.
LoadFiles checks the embedded app.pak SHA-256, decompresses gzip, then reads length-prefixed asset records into memory; it does not load an assembly or execute a dropped binary.
The generated 32-byte device key is protected/unprotected with DPAPI CurrentUser. It wraps this application's encrypted IndexedDB vault, rather than extracting existing credentials.

Handle enforces loopback Host names and rejects cross-site sensitive requests. /save also requires POST and X-Atoms:1. SafeTarget restricts writes to the app's Pictures/Documents subfolders and rejects path traversal, invalid components, and device names.
EndOtherCopies uses WMI to select the current executable basename, excludes its own PID, and terminates only matching-port copies after listener binding fails.
RegisterProtocol writes the current executable as the per-user atoms: URL handler. MakeDesktopShortcut creates a visible desktop link; neither is a startup trigger.

Decoded 10968 string-table calls using only isolated decoder/rotation/arithmetic wrappers in QuickJS, then traced the recovered UI, session handshake, received-message dispatch, file sharing, backups, calls, updates, and plugins.

Peer sessions derive AES-GCM keys using static/ephemeral ECDH and HKDF, require invite/contact admission, and transfer app posts/messages and selected media. No credential collection or arbitrary native-command dispatch found.

The app fetches same-publisher version metadata and offers a user-clicked installer download. Catalog plugins are hash-checked and mounted as sandbox=allow-scripts frames with connect-src/frame-src none; additional permissions default off.

packaging.authenticode: Absent, verified with osslsigncode; a matching embedded resource hash is not publisher authentication.
packaging.obfuscation: Commercial-style JavaScript identifier mangling, rotated string arrays, custom Base64 alphabet, and decoder wrappers; compressed as ordinary gzip.
packaging.deployment_context: Standalone executable supplied without an invite, provisioned peer, installer, execution command line, or host activity. Intent of a particular deployment cannot be established.

external_checks.result: Current 1.10.2 distribution corroborates the product and architecture; it is a different release, not an exact reference for 1.7.1. Core launcher methods Main, Fail, Run, ReadArgs, LoadFiles are byte-identical IL with version/resource constants stored separately.
Version 1.10.2, released 2026-10-20, points to a same-origin installer; no automatic launcher execution path.

Fetched and inspected the currently listed Atom Math Lab package. Its listed SHA-256 matches downloaded bytes; arithmetic-game logic, local helper and SVG icon, with no network or native execution found.

why_collected: External corpus and 12/71 scanner flags establish provenance, not behavior. Unsigned small-app distribution, high-entropy gzip assets, extensive JavaScript obfuscation, DPAPI, process termination and network APIs plausibly explain heuristic detections. The actual collection or deployment reason remains unknown.
trait_changes: Add declared product/manifest identity and a corroborated Atom's Connections application identity; these do not suppress any behavior.
Recognize relative as well as rooted/escaped shell-open-command subpaths; include DLLs and reject commander suffix near misses.
Add a general .NET URL-handler registration API/key-reference composite at notable severity, without inferring hijacking or persistence.
control_method: Equal-length mutations of supplied PE product and manifest identity strings, and URL Protocol value-name string. Separately test relative/rooted/escaped subpaths and the shell/open/commander near miss in batch fixtures. Stored under the task scratch directory, alongside CIL, decoded JavaScript, upstream files and scan reports.
scan_status: Initial and final atomscan completed; targeted test-rules matched identity, URL-handler references and shell-open-command; final scan has zero hostile and zero suspicious findings.
